committees.name: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects participants in defined contribution retirement plans by removing compensation exclusions and raising emergency savings caps, plus grant recipients.
dimensions.evidence: means an individual, without regard to whether the individual is otherwise a participant in such plan, who meets any age, service, and other eligibility requirements

dimensions.assessment: Increases the maximum emergency savings account contribution limit to $5,000 and expands access to highly compensated employees previously excluded.
Appropriates explicit discretionary and mandatory funding amounts for the Employee Ownership Initiative Grant Program ranging from millions annually through FY2035.
dimensions.evidence: For fiscal year 2027, $8,000,000... For fiscal year 2028, $10,000,000

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, and the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022.
dimensions.evidence: Section 801 of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (29 U.S.C. 1193) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent retirement account rule changes starting in 2027 and funding authorizations extending through fiscal year 2035.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by sections 2 and 3 shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026.

missing_information: Exact tax revenue impact estimates resulting from changes to savings account contribution limits.
importance_detail.rationale: Modifies pension-linked emergency savings accounts by expanding eligibility, doubling the participant contribution maximum to $5,000, and funding employee ownership grants through FY2035.
